clue.text: Left hands?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the left-wing political party in Britain
second meaning: hired hands, the workforce

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a question about which hand is the left one; the two words are separate meanings. Britain's Labour Party is the main party of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the British party of the left and the body of workers employed, as in manual hands.

clue.text: Island church has character

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A small island boasts a church with plenty of local character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a quality of the church, but it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: AITCH is the spelled-out name of the letter H, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Submission for honour in case review is required

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again and rework it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone must bow and submit before an honour is granted, in case the award is reviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deference or bowing, a show of submission to authority.

clue.text: Another drink could make 11 sick

parts.note: the answer to 11 across names one who blows a whistle, which a referee does
ill is a synonym for sick

explanation.surface: One more drink might make someone feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at WHISTLER, a nickname for a referee, shortened to REF.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a second glass topped up again, so it is another drink poured.

clue.text: Set from abroad, just edited

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the words that follow, unchanged

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A text set in type overseas has just been edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' looks like part of the definition, but it only supplies the last two letters of the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a clock or instrument is to adjust it to the right position or value.

clue.text: Is it all, say, plain sailing aboard this vessel?

definitions.text: Is it all, say, plain sailing aboard this vessel?

parts.words: Is it all, say, plain sailing aboard this vessel?
parts.note: surface reading: asking whether a voyage on some ship is easy and trouble-free
setter's reading: 'say' marks plain as a sound-alike for plane, so the ship sails with aeroplanes aboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain sailing' is an idiom for something easy; read with 'say' it becomes planes sailing on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This warship carries aircraft on its flight deck, so planes go to sea aboard it.

clue.text: Representative of English king gets papal edict

parts.note: King John of England, of Magna Carta fame
a bull is a formal decree issued by the Pope

explanation.surface: An English king receives a decree from the Pope, as King John famously did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English king' seems a unit, but 'English' belongs to the definition. John Bull is the stock cartoon figure personifying England.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the stout cartoon character who personifies England and the typical Englishman.

clue.text: Number in second eleven the Spanish got out

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: what has got out has left, so those letters are removed from the word they were in

parts.note: taken as written
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A number in a cricket club's second eleven was dismissed by the Spanish side.
explanation.walkthrough: A second eleven is a club's reserve team; the clue reads as a cricket score, but 'second' is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, the whole number between six and eight.

clue.text: Segregate, oddly, for holiday eating

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Diners are oddly split up for a holiday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are a treat eaten at the Easter holiday, so they are seasonal holiday food.

clue.text: Pilot away from home? He was drowned in Dickens's novel

definitions.text: He was drowned in Dickens's novel

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
to go forth is to go away from home, out into the world

explanation.surface: Steering a ship away from home ends in drowning, as for a character in Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long tail: Steerforth is the charming friend in David Copperfield who drowns in a storm off Yarmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: James Steerforth, David Copperfield's schoolfriend, dies in a shipwreck near Yarmouth late in the novel.

clue.text: Match cut for this garment

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed short, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a vesta is a short wax match, a once-common British name

explanation.surface: A match is used to cut up a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game or a pairing; here it is the striking kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is an undershirt in Britain, or a waistcoat in America, either way a garment.

clue.text: Bird painter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: any of several birds named for their whistling call
second meaning: James McNeill ..., the American painter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a painter of birds; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler is both the name for whistling birds such as the golden whistler and the surname of the artist of Whistler's Mother.

clue.text: Chap requiring cake and endless tea? Right

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
taken as written before shortening
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man who always wants cake and endless tea, and is right to.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, forever after cakes and tea, so the whole clue paints him.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunter is a named fellow from British school stories, and chap is an informal word for any man.

clue.text: Tips to back these two horses

indicators.note: putting something to the back reverses its order, so the word runs from end to start

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident tip

explanation.surface: A racing tip to back a pair of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' sounds like betting on the horses, which suits the racing picture, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a matched pair of horses or oxen harnessed together to draw a vehicle.

clue.text: Theatrical parts in 100 operas, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters are one possible arrangement among many, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: The stage roles in a hundred operas or so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical parts' suggests roles; it means parts of a theatre building.
explanation.definitionFit: A proscenium is the part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain, framed by the arch.

clue.text: Collapse with winter setting in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tumble to the ground
second meaning, read cryptically: when autumn, the American fall, is over, winter arrives

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' is the American word for autumn, so the phrase split in two describes the season ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall over is to topple and collapse; split apart it says autumn has ended.

clue.text: Slightly unconventional, and in the red?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a little odd or eccentric
second meaning, read cryptically: a red is left-wing, away from the political middle

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the red' wants to mean in debt; here red is political, a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-centre means quirky or eccentric, and literally a left-wing red sits away from the political middle ground.

clue.text: Citizen's articles about Northern Ireland

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the following letters are enclosed

parts.note: the English articles a, the and an, run together
standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A citizen writes newspaper articles about Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests pieces of journalism, but means the grammatical words a, the and an.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian is a native or citizen of Athens, the ancient city-state or modern Greek capital.

clue.text: Home-made answer to anagram for Times crossword's number one

parts.note: to answer a purpose is to serve or do, as in that will do

indicators.note: the setter says outright that the following word is to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
the first letter of crossword

explanation.surface: A homespun solution to the anagram that leads off the Times crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself, setting a Times anagram in the Times. 'Number one' picks out the first letter, not a clue number.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic goods are produced at home rather than imported, so home-made in the national sense.

clue.text: Obscure-sounding round-the-world traveller

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so the word is spelt to match what you hear, not the meaning

parts.note: to fog is to obscure or blur

explanation.surface: An obscure-sounding globetrotter.
explanation.walkthrough: Phileas Fogg is the hero of Jules Verne's Around the World in Eighty Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Phileas Fogg wagers he can circle the globe in eighty days in Verne's novel.

clue.text: Takes off clothes for games

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is a plural of strip
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a team's sports kit, called a strip in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings share the word 'clothes'. In Britain a football team's strip is its kit of shirt, shorts and socks.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to undress, and strips are the matching uniforms sports teams wear in games.

clue.text: Rare present person hasn't made himself

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: someone still here has not made himself this, from the idiom for leaving

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make yourself scarce' means go away, so someone still present has failed to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means seldom found or in short supply, and to make yourself scarce is idiom for departing.

clue.text: Disputed what the crew did? Doesn't sound like it
Make short work of Sappers?

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a trench is the kind of earthwork sappers dig

explanation.surface: Army engineers make quick work of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make short work of' is an idiom for finishing fast, but it splits: 'Make short' is the definition, 'work of Sappers' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back or reduce spending, making a budget shorter.

clue.text: Bishop may take this piece after chess opening

indicators.note: after says the piece named first is placed second, behind the other
an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of chess
a rook is a chess piece, the castle

explanation.surface: In chess, a bishop may capture a piece just after the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: this bishop is a churchman, who carries a hooked staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a bishop's hooked pastoral staff, also called a crozier, carried in ceremonies.

clue.text: Kent gardens round centre of Sevenoaks

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: Kew Gardens, the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one used

parts.note: the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: Gardens in Kent near the town of Sevenoaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county, home to Sevenoaks; it is an old Scots past tense of ken, to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken means to know in Scots, and kent is its past tense, equivalent to the standard form.

clue.text: Start one after it in one race

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following ones

parts.note: one is I, and a race of people is a nation
taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral, placed after

explanation.surface: A runner starts after the first one in a single race.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'one after it' puts I after IT; that pair then sits inside I plus NATION, just after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiation is a beginning or start, especially the launch of a scheme or entry into a group.

clue.text: Traveller to Canterbury going further than commuter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of Chaucer's pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales
second meaning, read cryptically: one who commutes a sentence only lessens it, while this person cancels it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commuter' suggests a daily rail traveller, which suits a trip to Canterbury, but here it means someone who reduces a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Pardoner sells indulgences on the pilgrimage, and one who forgives entirely goes beyond merely reducing a punishment.

clue.text: Arab leader's instant pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is the one heard aloud

parts.note: a shake is a moment, as in two shakes

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler makes a snap declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective for the pronouncement, but it is a noun meaning a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikh is the chief or head of an Arab tribe, family or village.
